package_info.package_manager: N/A (malicious Windows executable, not a package manager ecosystem)
package_info.why_malicious: QNodeService is a newly discovered Trojan distributed via Coronavirus-themed phishing campaigns. It is designed to provide remote access to infected systems, enabling attackers to exfiltrate data, execute commands, and maintain persistence. The malware is delivered as a malicious file attachment, masquerading as a COVID-19 tax relief document, and is executed by unsuspecting victims.

execution_context.file_location: malicious executable delivered via phishing email

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The Trojan establishes a connection to a command-and-control (C2) server, allowing remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands, upload/download files, and exfiltrate sensitive data.
malicious_snippets.code_language: javascript (Node.js, as implied by the name QNodeService)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code connects to a remote C2 server, receives commands, executes them on the victim's machine, and sends results or stolen data back to the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Establishing a remote connection to a C2 server and allowing arbitrary command execution is a hallmark of backdoor Trojans.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal software does not open remote command channels or exfiltrate data without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote administration tools (RATs) used in enterprise IT, but with user awareness and consent.
key_indicators: Outbound connection to attacker-controlled C2 server
Ability to execute arbitrary commands remotely

attack_chain.action: Victim receives a phishing email promising COVID-19 tax relief with a malicious attachment.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim opens the attachment and executes the malware.

attack_chain.action: Malicious QNodeService executable runs on the victim's machine.
Malware connects to C2 server, receives commands, and exfiltrates data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains remote control and can steal data or further compromise the system.

behavioral_signatures: Execution of unknown Node.js-based binaries from email attachments
Outbound connections to known C2 infrastructure after opening suspicious files
Unusual process spawning and command execution initiated by user document interaction
file_indicators: Unexpected executable attachments with COVID-19 or tax relief themes
Files named to appear as official documents but containing Node.js or JavaScript code
network_indicators: Connections to attacker-controlled C2 domains or IPs
Unusual outbound traffic immediately after opening document attachments
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for execution of Node.js or JavaScript-based binaries originating from email attachments, especially those with COVID-19 or financial relief themes. Detect outbound connections to known C2 infrastructure or anomalous domains following document execution. Alert on processes spawned by document viewers (e.g., Word, PDF readers) that initiate network connections or execute scripts.
